column1: # Shared XDG_* absoluteness vectors. On Unix (Linux, macOS, WSL) an
# XDG_* value is honoured iff it starts with `/`; Windows spellings, relative
# paths, `~`, empty and leading-space values are ignored. Read by the Rust test:
# Format: one vector per line, tab-separated: value<TAB>absolute (yes|no).
# Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored. `value` uses the mini
# escape scheme of cache_key_vectors.tsv (\\ -> one backslash) plus the single
# whole-column token \e meaning the EMPTY string. Every reader MUST fail if this file is
# the value iff `absolute` is yes, and each of `runtime_root_for`,
# `cache_root_for` and `config_root_for` either roots at `value/gpy` or falls
# through as if the value were unset.
# Rust also replays each row with NO usable home (a relative HOME):
# then an unhonoured value leaves nothing usable, and the runtime root, the
# cache root and the config root must all fail to resolve, never fall back to
